The card also boasts advanced cybersecurity solutions and privacy protections, including specific measures to prevent fraudulent activity and ensure user data is not sold to third parties.

title: An insight into procurement at Apple Inc.
summary: This article explores Apple Inc.'s procurement strategies, highlighting its rigorous supplier standards and commitment to a diverse supplier base. It details how Apple requires its suppliers to align with its culture, innovation values, and social responsibilities. The piece also outlines the process for becoming an Apple supplier and the initiatives of its Supplier Diversity Programme, established in 1993.

title: C.H. Robinson launches Navisphere on Apple, Andriod
summary: C.H. Robinson has launched its Navisphere platform on Apple and Android smartphones, significantly extending its global reach. This new app allows users to access detailed shipment information, track movements, view documents, and contact account representatives directly. The move reinforces C.H. Robinson's commitment to mobile technology, building on previous mobile app developments for carriers.

title: Premium Calm meditation app membership now included on American Express cards
summary: American Express has launched a new perk offering a complimentary one-year premium membership to the Calm meditation and sleep app for all its US personal card members, starting May 18. This membership, normally costing $69.99 annually, can be extended for a second year at 50% off with automatic renewal, and also applies to American Express corporate cards. This initiative aims to provide valuable well-being resources during stressful times and enhance the appeal of Amex's personal card lineup, although business cards are not eligible.

title: Why Intel is betting its chips on microprocessor mastermind Jim Keller
summary: This article profiles Jim Keller, a legendary microprocessor designer who has worked for Apple, Tesla, and AMD, and is now tasked with revitalizing Intel's chip-design enterprise. It explores his unconventional career path, his philosophy of simplification and learning, and the significant impact his designs have had on the tech industry, including the Ryzen chips for AMD and the Autopilot chip for Tesla. The piece details how Intel is relying on Keller to overcome its recent struggles and regain its market leadership.

title: Apple checks in with 192-room hotel for billion-dollar Northwest Austin campus
summary: Apple updated its plans for its new $1 billion corporate campus in Northwest Austin to include a 192-room hotel. This addition is seen as a trendsetting move by corporate location consultant John Boyd Jr., who expects more companies to integrate hotels into their campuses, particularly after the COVID-19 pandemic, to enhance control over corporate travel and ensure traveler security. The campus, set to open in 2022, will eventually house up to 15,000 employees and will be Apple's largest hub outside its Cupertino headquarters.

title: Revised Apple campus site plan in Northwest Austin includes new 6-story hotel
summary: Apple Inc.'s revised site plan for its new Northwest Austin campus now includes a 6-story hotel featuring 192 rooms. The new campus, approved by the city on April 29, is located on a 133-acre tract and is expected to house up to 15,000 workers, with the first buildings projected to open in 2022. This expansion also highlights Apple's continued manufacturing presence in Northwest Austin, where Mac Pro computers are produced.

title: Different Market, Same Leaders: Tech ETFs Thrive In Pandemic
summary: In April 2020, even amidst market volatility and the COVID-19 pandemic, technology-focused ETFs led the recovery, echoing previous market trends. Direxion's leveraged tech ETFs, such as TECL, SOXL, and WEBL, showed significant gains, driven by strong performances in financial technology, semiconductor industries, and companies benefiting from increased online activity. This indicates a market belief that technology will continue to spearhead economic recovery despite overall uncertainty.

title: Fingerprint Sensor Market to Grow with 13.6% CAGR in Coming Years: P&S Intelligence
summary: The global fingerprint sensors market is projected to grow at a 13.6% CAGR between 2020 and 2030, driven by increasing security concerns and the rising integration of fingerprint-sensing technology in smartphones and other consumer electronics. Area/touch sensors, particularly those based on capacitive technology, are expected to experience the fastest demand growth. Asia-Pacific is forecasted to be the region with the highest CAGR, propelled by government initiatives and the booming population's adoption of smart devices.

title: Same Old Leadership Song Lifts These Leveraged ETFs
summary: Technology sector leadership is driving the stock market's recovery from March lows, benefiting leveraged ETFs like Direxion Daily Technology Bull 3X Shares (NYSE: TECL) and Direxion Daily Dow Jones Internet Bull 3X Shares (NYSE: WEBL). TECL is a triple-leveraged play on Microsoft and Apple, while WEBL offers a similar leveraged exposure to internet giants like Amazon, Facebook, and Netflix. Both ETFs have seen significant gains and investor interest due to the strong performance of their underlying tech and internet components.

title: Roberto Escobar, former Medellín Cartel accountant, sues Apple for $2.6 billion, report says
summary: Roberto Escobar, brother of Pablo Escobar and former Medellín Cartel accountant, is suing Apple for $2.6 billion. He claims an iPhone security flaw exposed his address via FaceTime, leading to threats and relocation. This lawsuit coincides with Escobar's marketing efforts for his own line of gold-plated iPhones and a website criticizing Apple.

title: This Rugged Safari-Style Defender Is Resto-Modding Done Right
summary: ECD Automotive Design has transformed a Land Rover Defender 90 into a rugged safari-style vehicle, combining luxury and utility. This resto-mod features a Chevy LS3 V8 engine, upgraded Fox suspension, Nappa leather interior, and a Coniston Green paint job, making it ideal for summer adventures.

title: San Jose-based Cisco promises $5M for charities fighting racism, discrimination
summary: Cisco Systems Inc. announced it would donate $5 million to charities combating racism and discrimination, following widespread protests over racial injustice. Other tech companies like Facebook, Intel, and Apple have also pledged similar contributions. This decision led Cisco to postpone its annual Cisco Live event, with CEO Chuck Robbins emphasizing the need for space and healing amid current societal turmoil.

title: Apple begins to sell Sonos as the speaker company accuses Google and Amazon of patent theft
summary: Apple has started selling the Sonos One SL Wireless Speaker online and in its stores. This comes as Sonos has publicly sued Google and accused Amazon of patent theft related to its streaming technology. The Sonos One SL speaker can stream Apple Music via Siri or AirPlay 2.

title: Fidelity Blue Chip Growth ETF Holdings
summary: This article details the holdings of the Fidelity Blue Chip Growth ETF (FBCG), an actively-managed, non-transparent fund focusing on large-cap global growth stocks. Established on June 3, 2020, FBCG manages $5393.83 million in assets across 196 holdings, with top investments including NVIDIA, Apple, Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft. The article also provides recent changes in the ETF's shareholdings as of the end of May and June 2022.

title: Intel loses ‘rock star’ chip designer Jim Keller
summary: Intel Corp. has announced the departure of its celebrated chip designer, Jim Keller, who is leaving for "personal reasons" after two years with the company. Keller, known for his work at AMD, Apple, and Tesla, was instrumental in Intel's efforts to expand beyond traditional PC and server chips into new markets like AI and cloud computing. Despite his departure, Intel has already reorganized its engineering leadership and Keller will serve as a consultant for six months to ensure a smooth transition.

title: Former Apple executive Jim Keller resigns from top chip design role at Intel
summary: Jim Keller, a prominent chip designer known for his work at Apple, Tesla, and AMD, has resigned from his role at Intel for personal reasons. His departure raises concerns among analysts about Intel's processor roadmap and vulnerability to competition, especially with Apple reportedly planning to use its own chips in Macs. Keller will serve as a consultant for Intel for six months during the transition.

title: Intel Loses a Chip Wizard at the Worst Possible Time
summary: Intel's top chip architect, Jim Keller, resigned effective immediately for personal reasons after only two years with the company. This departure is seen as a significant blow to Intel, which is already ceding ground to rivals in a competitive market, and comes at a challenging time for the chip giant. Keller's extensive experience from companies like Apple and AMD highlights the severity of his exit for Intel.

title: Apple, ARM, and Intel
summary: This article discusses Apple's anticipated transition of its Mac computers from Intel processors to its own ARM-based chips, highlighting the historical context of this decision, Intel's manufacturing struggles, and the potential implications for performance and the broader server market. It also critically examines Intel's past strategic missteps, particularly its decision regarding iPhone chip production.

title: This NAACP-backed ETF will help you invest in companies that care about equality
summary: The Impact Shares NAACP Minority Empowerment ETF (NACP) allows investors to support companies committed to diversity and racial equality. Developed in partnership with the NAACP and Impact Shares, the ETF screens companies based on their practices in hiring, pay, promotion, and supply chains, with net proceeds going to the NAACP for social advocacy. With over $4 million in net assets and holdings in major companies like Amazon and Microsoft, the fund aims to achieve "social alpha" by investing in corporate leaders in social justice.

title: After 15 Years, Apple Prepares to Break Up With Intel (Published 2020)
summary: Apple is preparing to end its 15-year partnership with Intel, with plans to replace Intel processors in Macs with self-designed chips. This move, expected to be announced soon, signifies Apple's growing independence and determination to control its product manufacturing, a trend seen among other major tech companies like Facebook, Amazon, and Google. The new Mac chips are anticipated to arrive next year and will likely be manufactured by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing.

title: Xtrackers MSCI Kokusai Equity ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:KOKU)
summary: The Xtrackers MSCI Kokusai Equity ETF (KOKU) tracks a market cap-weighted index of large and mid-cap developed market stocks globally, excluding Japan. Launched on April 8, 2020, KOKU has $823.01 million in market capitalization and a net expense ratio of 0.09%. Its top holdings include major tech companies like Apple, NVIDIA, and Microsoft.

title: Dan IVES Wedbush AI Revolution ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:IVES) $IVES
summary: This article provides details on the Dan IVES Wedbush AI Revolution ETF (NYSEARCA:IVES), including its current price, holdings, and news. As of June 17, 2026, the fund is trading at $37.37, up 18.2% year-to-date, and has key holdings in major tech companies like Micron, Taiwan Semiconductor, NVIDIA, and Apple. The ETF focuses on information technology equities related to cloud technology companies and has an aggregate rating of "Moderate Buy."

title: Trump signs order freezing visas for foreign workers through the end of the year
summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order freezing new visas for various foreign workers, including tech and low-skill jobs, through the end of 2020. This action, aiming to preserve jobs amidst the COVID-19 economic downturn, exempts specific essential workers but includes au pairs and certain other exchange programs. The policy is expected to face backlash from the business community and immigration advocates despite the White House's claim of saving or creating 525,000 American jobs.

title: Apple, Google and chorus of tech business leaders slam Trump's new visa restrictions
summary: Tech giants Apple and Google, along with other prominent business leaders, criticized the Trump administration's new restrictions on work visas, including the H-1B and L-1 visas. Critics argue that these restrictions, implemented to free up jobs for American workers, will actually hinder job creation and economic growth. CEOs like Tim Cook, Sundar Pichai, Brad Smith, Marc Benioff, and Elon Musk all expressed disappointment, highlighting the positive contributions of immigrant workers to innovation and the U.S. economy.

title: Apple buys Fleetsmith, a company making it easier to deploy iPhones and Macs at workplaces
summary: Apple has acquired Fleetsmith, a company specializing in tools for deploying and managing corporate iPhones and Macs. This acquisition aims to strengthen Apple's offerings in the enterprise market, a sector Apple CEO Tim Cook previously called the "mother of all opportunities." Fleetsmith's mobile device management software helps businesses remotely configure and manage Apple devices for their workforce.

title: Apple to Drop Intel and Use its own Chips in Mac Computers
summary: Apple announced its decision to transition from using Intel-based chips to its own Apple Silicon chips for its Mac computers, with the first Macs featuring these new chips expected by late 2020. This move aims to enhance Mac performance, efficiency, and establish a common architecture across all Apple products, allowing Mac computers to run apps previously exclusive to iPhones and iPads. The new Apple chips are based on technology from Arm Holdings, whose technology also powers the world's fastest supercomputer, Fugaku.

title: 3 ETFs With Rising Profit Forecasts
summary: Despite a challenging economic environment and a potential second wave of COVID-19, some ETFs are showing rising earnings forecasts. The ETF Research Center identified three such funds: the Brand Value ETF (BVAL), the Roundhill BITKRAFT Esports & Digital Entertainment ETF (NERD), and the VanEck Vectors Environmental Services ETF (EVX), which are seeing positive revisions in their component companies' 2020 earnings estimates, indicating resilience and growth potential in their respective sectors.

title: Software Maker for Apple Devices Jamf Files for U.S. IPO
Santander appoints three leading technologists to support its strategy and digital transformation
summary: Santander has appointed R. Martin Chávez, Sebastian Gunningham, and Francisco D’Souza to key roles to bolster its digital transformation. Chávez will join the board as an independent director, Gunningham will chair Santander Consumer Finance and become vice chairman of Openbank, and D’Souza will be a strategic advisor for Santander Global Platform. These appointments aim to leverage their extensive technology and financial sector experience to drive Santander's digital strategy.

title: Here’s what Spotify, Live Nation, Sony, Warner and other music companies are paying women compared to men in the UK
summary: This article details the UK gender pay gap statistics for major music companies like Sony Music, Warner Music, Spotify, Apple, and Live Nation, based on data as of April 5, 2019. It breaks down the average hourly pay difference and bonus disparities between male and female employees, as well as the gender split across different pay quartiles for each company. The report highlights that while some companies, like Spotify, have a smaller gap, others like Live Nation show significant disparities in pay and bonuses.

title: Walmart Just Made a Bold Move That Families Are Going to Love. It's a Lesson in Emotional Intelligence
summary: Walmart launched two initiatives, "Camp by Walmart" and "Walmart Drive-In," to provide safe entertainment for families during the Covid-19 pandemic. These moves demonstrate emotional intelligence by addressing a key customer need and strengthening relationships with budget-conscious families. The article suggests that businesses of all sizes can learn from Walmart's approach by identifying and filling customer needs to build stronger brand connections.

title: Smart investment during a pandemic
summary: Franklin Templeton advocates for a well-diversified global investment portfolio to navigate market uncertainties during a pandemic. They suggest adopting "Defend, Diversify, and Buffer" strategies to protect investments and seize opportunities in sectors like technology and emerging markets. The article emphasizes long-term trends and the benefits of professional fund management over market timing.

title: Report: Apple Testing QR Codes With Apple Pay
summary: Apple Inc. is reportedly testing QR codes as an alternative technology for Apple Pay, as a hidden feature in the iOS 14 beta suggests users may soon be able to make payments by scanning QR or traditional barcodes. This move could broaden mobile payments beyond NFC, particularly in international markets where QR codes are prevalent, though it raises questions about Apple's commitment to its proprietary payment infrastructure. While NFC is considered more secure, QR codes offer lower cost and broader accessibility, especially in developing countries.

title: Gilead to expand Irish operations, approx 40 jobs to be created in Cork
summary: Gilead Sciences, Inc. announced plans to create 140 new jobs in Ireland, with approximately 40 of these positions to be located in Cork. The company, which already has drug product manufacturing operations and a financial shared services center in Cork, is expanding its presence in areas such as clinical development, process development, and analytical operations. Recruitment is underway, with 80 roles expected to be filled within 12 months and the remainder by early 2022.

title: New Joker variant hits Google Play with an old trick
summary: Check Point Research has identified a new variant of the Joker malware, a premium dialer and dropper spyware, on Google Play. This variant employs an older PC-based technique of hiding its malicious dex file using Base64 encoding to evade detection. The malware allows unauthorized subscription to premium services, and Check Point advises users to uninstall infected apps, check bills, and install security solutions.

title: iPhone users can now get a first look at the biggest changes coming to their phones this fall
summary: Apple released a public beta of iOS 14, allowing iPhone users to preview upcoming changes before the official launch in the fall with new iPhone models. Key new features include a redesigned home screen with widgets, an App Library for automatic app organization, picture-in-picture video, less intrusive call notifications, a new Siri interface, a built-in Translate app, web page translation in Safari, new Memoji avatars, and iMessage improvements. While the beta may contain bugs, it offers an early look at significant updates for tech enthusiasts.

title: Nokia launches data center switches, routers, and networking OS; scores Apple, Equinix, and BT deals
summary: Nokia has introduced a new Data Center Fabric Solution comprising routers, a Network Operating System (NOS) called SR Linux, and an Automation and Operations toolkit. This new hardware range aims to automate and simplify data center operations, competing in a $12 billion market. Key customers like Apple, Equinix, and BT have already adopted Nokia's new data center networking products.

title: Apple CEO Tim Cook No.2 on 2019 highest paid list at $133.7 million
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook ranked second on the 2019 highest-paid executive list with $133.7 million, largely due to an equity grant he received in 2011. Elon Musk topped the list with $595.3 million, primarily from a pay deal tied to Tesla's valuation. The article highlights the significant compensation packages in the tech industry compared to other sectors like finance.

title: American Century Sustainable Equity ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:ESGA)
summary: The American Century Sustainable Equity ETF (ESGA) is an actively managed, non-transparent ETF that screens US companies using fundamental measures and ESG metrics. Launched on July 13, 2020, ESGA had assets under management of $238.68 million and a net expense ratio of 0.39% as of the article's last update. The fund's top holdings include major tech companies like Microsoft, Apple, NVIDIA, and Alphabet.

title: COVID-19 Impact & Recovery Analysis- Beacon Market
summary: Technavio predicts the beacon market will grow by $15.99 billion between 2020 and 2024, with a CAGR of nearly 57%, despite the impact of COVID-19. Key players include Apple Inc., Google LLC, and Texas Instruments Inc. The growth is primarily attributed to the increasing adoption of premium smartphones in emerging economies, though data security concerns pose a challenge.

title: SoftBank hires Goldman Sachs to explore sale options for chip designer Arm after getting inbound interest, sources say
summary: SoftBank has engaged Goldman Sachs to explore strategies for its chip designer unit, Arm Holdings, including a potential IPO or a direct sale. This move comes after SoftBank received unsolicited interest in Arm, which it acquired for approximately $32 billion in 2016. The Japanese tech conglomerate is seeking to raise cash to support its Vision Fund companies and plans to sell up to $41 billion in assets.

title: Is the Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund the Best Way to Invest in Tech?
summary: The Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK) is a popular ETF for tech exposure but may not be the most diversified option. Despite low operating expenses, XLK has a concentrated allocation with over 43% in Microsoft and Apple, covering only 71 companies. The PowerShares QQQ Trust (QQQ) offers broader diversification across 100 tech-focused names, providing a more balanced alternative even with a slightly higher expense ratio.

title: Charles Schwab says retail trading kept booming in second quarter amid market comeback
summary: Charles Schwab reported a significant surge in retail trading activity and new accounts in the second quarter of 2020, with 1.62 million daily active trades and 1.6 million new accounts added, including 1.1 million from the USAA acquisition. Despite this growth, the company missed analyst estimates for both revenue and earnings per share, primarily due to a decline in net interest revenue. Schwab also made "significant progress" on its pending acquisition of TD Ameritrade.

title: Barr condemns Disney and Hollywood for 'kowtowing' to China | William Barr
summary: US Attorney General William Barr criticized Disney and other Hollywood studios for allegedly "kowtowing" to the Chinese Communist Party, accusing them of prioritizing short-term profits over American values. Barr highlighted instances where Disney reportedly apologized for a film about the Dalai Lama and allowed Chinese officials a role in Shanghai Disneyland, while Hollywood studios allegedly tweaked scripts to appease Beijing. He also extended his criticism to US technology companies, calling them "pawns of Chinese influence" for their operations in China.

title: Apple teams up with HBCUs to bring coding and creativity opportunities to communities across the US
summary: Apple is expanding its Community Education Initiative by partnering with an additional 10 Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs). These partnerships will create regional coding centers that serve as technology hubs for campuses and their broader communities, offering opportunities in coding, creativity, and workforce development. This effort aims to advance educational equity and increase the representation of Black students and women in STEM and technology fields.

title: Big Tech Has a Big Climate Problem. Now, It’s Being Forced to Clean Up.
summary: Apple has pledged to make its devices carbon-neutral by 2030, joining other tech giants like Microsoft and Amazon in ramping up climate targets. The company plans to reduce emissions by 75% in its manufacturing chain through recycling and encouraging renewable energy use by suppliers, offsetting the remaining 25% with reforestation projects. These voluntary commitments come as big tech faces increasing pressure to address its own contribution to climate change.

title: New in July 2020: Playback Improvements for H.264 and HEVC on Windows
summary: Adobe has released updates for Premiere Pro and After Effects, significantly improving H.264 and HEVC playback performance on Windows Intel systems, offering up to a 2X speed increase due to collaboration with Intel. The update also introduces ProRes 4444 XQ export for macOS, previously Windows-only, and features the Roto Brush 2 in After Effects Beta, which uses Adobe Sensei for faster rotoscoping. These enhancements are part of Adobe's ongoing efforts to boost application quality and performance through strategic partnerships.

title: Jamf's stock soars in its public debut, after IPO prices above expectations
summary: Jamf Holding Corp.'s stock made a strong public debut, with shares opening 77% above its initial public offering price of $26, which was higher than expected. The company sold 18 million shares, raising $468 million, and was valued at $3.03 billion at the IPO price. This successful market entry occurred during a period of significant rallies for IPOs and the broader S&P 500.

title: Work From Home ETF Already Impressing
summary: The Direxion Work From Home ETF (WFH) has quickly gained over $50 million in assets and shown strong performance since its launch. The fund invests in companies across four technology pillars related to remote work and is seen as a credible long-term investment. WFH's underlying index has a higher price-to-sales multiple than the S&P 500 but a discount to the Nasdaq-100, with strong forecasted earnings growth.

title: Qualcomm Quarterly Revenue by Segment
summary: The article analyzes Qualcomm's quarterly revenue by segment from Q1 2005 to Q2 2020, highlighting that the QCT semiconductor business accounted for 78.6% of total revenue in fiscal Q2 2020. It details the performance of Qualcomm's QCT, QTL, and QSI segments, noting a significant decline in QSI due to an impairment loss related to OneWeb's bankruptcy. The report explains the factors driving segment-specific revenue changes.

title: Tesla deal could make US blacklisted Israeli billionaire richer
summary: Tesla's agreement to buy cobalt from Glencore could indirectly benefit Israeli billionaire Dan Gertler, who has been blacklisted from the US financial system since 2017. Gertler is entitled to royalties from Glencore's Congolese mines, which will supply most of Tesla's cobalt, raising ethical and potential legal concerns for the US company. This arrangement highlights the complexities of sourcing minerals from regions with human rights issues and corruption risks.

title: Corning unveils Gorilla Glass Victus with enhanced drop, scratch resistance
summary: Corning has introduced Gorilla Glass Victus, a new version of its popular glass that offers significant improvements in both drop and scratch resistance compared to its predecessor, Gorilla Glass 6. Lab tests show Victus surviving 2-meter drops and handling an 8 Newton load in scratch tests. While Apple uses Gorilla Glass, Samsung will be the first to incorporate Victus into a new device.

title: A newer, stronger version of Gorilla Glass is coming and Samsung will be the first company to use it
summary: Corning has announced Gorilla Glass Victus, an upgraded version of its smartphone display glass that boasts improved drop and scratch resistance. Victus can reportedly withstand drops from up to two meters and is twice as scratch-resistant as Gorilla Glass 6. Samsung will be the first company to integrate this new glass into its devices in the near future.

title: Gold Is Within Striking Distance of Its All-Time High. Here’s How to Play the Rally
summary: The article discusses gold's rally, nearing its all-time high, driven by the ongoing pandemic, global stimulus packages, and the overvaluation of tech stocks. Author Frank Holmes suggests that the precious metal is in a secular bull market and recommends a 10% portfolio weighting in gold and precious metals. He also highlights the strong performance of precious metal miners and royalty/streaming companies.

title: Koss Corp. suing major headphone brands, including Apple, Bose, for patent infringement
summary: Koss Corp. has filed five lawsuits against major headphone brands, including Apple, Bose, JLAB Audio, Skullcandy Inc., and Plantronics Inc., alleging infringement of its wireless headphone technology patents. These patents stem from Koss's "Striva" project in the mid-2000s, which aimed to develop "truly wireless headphones." Koss is seeking damages and a ruling of willful infringement, which could triple the award amount, though a specific figure has not been disclosed.

title: Koss Sues Apple, Bose, Over Wireless Headphone Patents (2)
summary: Koss Corp. has filed a series of lawsuits in Texas federal court, alleging that Apple Inc., Bose Corp., Plantronics Inc., Skullcandy Inc., and JLab Audio infringe on its wireless headphone patents. The patents cover technology that Koss claims it pioneered, including internal microphones, touch controls, and Wi-Fi connectivity in headphones. These lawsuits assert that the widespread adoption of such features in modern wireless headphones infringes on Koss's early innovations.

title: Intel stock dives, investors ‘frustrated’ by new manufacturing defects
summary: Intel's stock plunged after the company announced significant manufacturing delays with its next-generation 7-nanometer processors, putting it a year behind schedule. This news, following previous delays with 10nm chips, frustrated investors despite strong second-quarter results. CEO Bob Swan admitted to manufacturing problems and revealed contingency plans to outsource chip production to rivals if Intel cannot meet its own technology goals.

title: Intel's 7nm is Broken, Company Announces Delay Until 2022, 2023
summary: Intel announced a significant delay in the rollout of its 7nm CPUs, pushing their debut to late 2022 or early 2023. This delay is attributed to a "defect mode" causing yield degradation, putting Intel approximately twelve months behind its internal targets for 7nm process. The company is now exploring contingency plans, including the use of third-party foundries for some components and entire chip designs, and plans to increase shipments of 10nm chips by 20%.

title: New Corning Gorilla Glass skips the 7 and goes straight to Victus
summary: Corning has announced its new Gorilla Glass Victus, which offers significant improvements in both drop and scratch resistance compared to previous generations, including Gorilla Glass 6. This new glass can survive drops from up to 2 meters and has twice the scratch resistance of its predecessor. Samsung is expected to be the first to incorporate Gorilla Glass Victus into its products.

title: Abbott receives FDA approval for neurostimulator-controlling iPhone app for personalizing therapies for pain, Parkinson's disease
summary: Abbott has received FDA approval for its new NeuroSphere Digital Care platform and patient controller app, allowing users to personalize neuromodulation therapies for chronic pain and movement disorders like Parkinson's disease via their iPhones. The app aims to enhance remote patient engagement and virtual connections with healthcare providers, eliminating the need for a separate programmer device. This approval builds on Abbott's existing neuromodulation devices and platforms, reflecting a shift towards digital health solutions during the pandemic.

title: Corning reveals Gorilla Glass Victus that can survive a six-foot drop
summary: Corning has unveiled Gorilla Glass Victus, a new iteration of its protective glass designed to withstand serious drops and resist scratches. This new glass can reportedly survive drops from up to 2 meters (6.5 feet), making it twice as tough as Gorilla Glass 6, and will be more resistant to impact damage. Gorilla Glass Victus is expected to be integrated into new Samsung devices first, likely with the Galaxy models slated for an August 5 reveal.

title: Charting a bull-trend pullback, S&P 500 ventures under the breakout point
summary: The S&P 500 has pulled back below its breakout point of 3,233, extending to deeper support around the 3,200 mark, amidst heightened China-U.S. diplomatic tensions. The early Friday session low of 3,202 matched this inflection point, making the weekly close significant for further insight. This occurs while the NASDAQ 100 is challenging trendline support and Apple has violated a key trendline, though the article advises against panic.

title: Boyd Gaming unveils mobile gaming app with nostalgic brand
summary: Boyd Gaming Corp. has launched a new mobile gaming app called Stardust Social Casino, leveraging its vintage Las Vegas Stardust brand to stand out in the competitive mobile gaming market. The app offers virtual versions of slot titles found on Boyd Gaming casino floors, primarily for entertainment, and allows members of its B Connected loyalty program to earn points for in-app purchases. This move aims to connect with existing customers and attract new players familiar with the historic Stardust brand.

title: Intel ousts its chief engineer, shakes up technical group after delays
summary: Intel Corp has announced the departure of its Chief Engineering Officer Murthy Renduchintala and a reorganization of its key technology unit into five teams. This move comes after delays in the company's 7-nanometer chip technology development, which was reported to be six months behind schedule. The new leaders of these teams will report directly to CEO Bob Swan, with veteran Ann Kelleher leading the 7-nanometer and 5-nanometer chip development.

title: Imax Workers' Early 'Tenet' Review: "Oh My God - I Forgot How Great It Was To Be In A Movie", CEO Relays
summary: Imax CEO Rich Gelfond shared early reactions from employees who saw Christopher Nolan's "Tenet," describing their overwhelming sense of joy at being in a movie theater again. The film, which was made with Imax equipment, is set to open internationally before its U.S. release with Imax expecting 90% of its global network to be open by August's end. Gelfond also discussed the safety protocols in place, emphasizing Imax's advantages over other venues in managing COVID-19 transmission riscos and addressed the Universal-AMC deal, stating it would not significantly impact Imax's business model.

title: Prudential and PAI Health enter partnership to deliver the new way to measure physical activity on digital health app, Pulse
summary: Prudential Corporation Asia and PAI Health have partnered to integrate PAI Health's Personal Activity Intelligence (PAI) score into Prudential's Pulse digital health app across 11 Asian markets. This collaboration aims to enhance customer engagement by providing a science-backed metric to measure physical activity and reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease mortality. Pulse users, with a compatible heart monitor wearable, will benefit from personalized guidance on physical activity, with the potential to extend lives.

title: Apple CEO Cook says his company is "uniquely American" with no "dominant market share"
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook will testify before the House Judiciary's Subcommittee on Antitrust, where he plans to argue that Apple is a "uniquely American company" that operates in a competitive marketplace without dominant market share. He will highlight the fierce competition in the smartphone market from companies like LG, Samsung, Huawei, and Google, and defend the App Store's model as beneficial for developers. Cook will assert that Apple has never increased its commissions and that its fees are comparable to or lower than those of competitors.

title: Apple tried to lure Amazon's video app by offering a lower 15% fee, email shows
summary: An email released by the House Antitrust Subcommittee revealed that Apple offered Amazon a reduced 15% revenue share for Amazon Prime Video subscriptions signed up through the app, a departure from Apple's standard 30% fee. This suggests that large companies may be able to negotiate more favorable business terms on the App Store, contradicting Apple's public statements about treating all developers equally. The revelation came during a Congressional hearing on Big Tech where Apple CEO Tim Cook testified.

title: Here’s what the CEOs of Apple, Amazon, Facebook and Alphabet will say at Wednesday’s antitrust hearing
summary: The CEOs of Apple, Amazon, Facebook, and Alphabet are scheduled to testify before a House antitrust panel on Wednesday. Their prepared statements indicate they will argue that competition exists and their companies strengthen America. The executives, including Jeff Bezos, Tim Cook, Mark Zuckerberg, and Sundar Pichai, will appear via videoconference.

title: Apple Halved App Store Fee to Get Amazon Prime Video on Devices
summary: Apple Inc. agreed in 2016 to reduce its App Store fee for Amazon.com Inc. by half for subscriptions obtained through its Prime Video app. This deal was a result of direct negotiations between Apple's Eddy Cue and Amazon's Jeff Bezos, aiming to bring the Prime Video app to Apple devices and its TV set-top box. The agreement specified a 15% revenue share for new subscribers via the app, with no share for existing Amazon Prime Video users.

title: PayPal Plots a POS Course With QR Codes As It Comes Off the ‘Strongest’ Quarter in Its History
summary: PayPal is significantly expanding its physical point-of-sale strategy by rolling out QR code payment acceptance, starting with a major deal with CVS Pharmacy to service all 8,000 stores by year-end. This move comes as the company reports its "strongest" quarter in history, driven by increased active accounts, payment volume, and revenue during the coronavirus pandemic. PayPal is also working with over 100 enterprise merchants in the U.S. and Europe to further integrate QR code payments, highlighting their strategic importance for daily use and future economic benefits.

title: Apple smashes revenue estimates in record third quarter
summary: Apple significantly surpassed revenue expectations in its fiscal third quarter, reporting a record $59.7 billion, an 11% increase year-over-year. This surge was driven by increased demand for iPhones, iPads, and Mac computers as consumers adapted to working and learning from home during the pandemic. The company also announced a four-for-one stock split and confirmed a slight delay for the next iPhone launch.

title: How manufacturer Flex navigated covid shutdowns to keep Apple products and Philips ventilators on the market
summary: This article details how Flex Ltd., a Singapore-based manufacturer, adapted to the COVID-19 pandemic's supply chain disruptions. Under CEO Revathi Advaithi, Flex rapidly re-engineered operations, relocated production, and leveraged technology to overcome shortages and continue manufacturing essential goods like Philips ventilators and Apple products. The crisis accelerated a trend towards less reliance on China and more regionalized production networks.

title: Apple Announces 4-1 Stock Split After Shares Surge Toward $400
summary: Apple Inc. announced a 4-for-1 stock split following a significant surge in its share price over the past year. The company stated this move aims to make the stock more accessible to a broader base of investors, with post-split trading beginning on August 31. This marks Apple's fifth stock split since going public in 1980, contrasting with other large tech companies that typically avoid such actions.

title: Move over Aramco, Apple is now world’s most valuable company
summary: Apple Inc. has surpassed Saudi Aramco to become the world's most valuable company, with its market capitalization reaching $1.817 trillion after a 10% jump on Friday. This shift comes as Apple has benefited from an accelerated move to digital services during the pandemic, while Aramco has faced challenges including a disappointing IPO and plunging crude prices. Apple's valuation now stands higher than Aramco's $1.76 trillion, highlighting the growing strength of tech companies amid global changes.

title: Dexcom makes controlling blood sugar far simpler for diabetes patients -- and everyone else too
summary: Dexcom's continuous glucose monitors (CGMs) are revolutionizing diabetes care by providing real-time blood sugar data, making it far simpler for patients to manage their condition. The latest G6 Pro model offers significant advancements, including smaller size, automatic monitoring, and smartphone integration, moving beyond traditional painful fingerstick methods. These devices not only empower diabetic patients to lead more normal lives but also show promise for non-diabetics interested in understanding their body's response to food and exercise.

title: Tim Cook says Apple buys innovation, not competitors
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook explained the company's acquisition strategy, stating that Apple buys companies for their technology and intellectual property, which are then integrated as features into existing products like the iPhone. He contrasted this approach with other tech giants, implying that Apple focuses on innovation rather than eliminating competitors. Cook cited examples such as Touch ID, Workflow (now Shortcuts), Texture (now Apple News+), FaceShift (now Animoji), Siri, and P.A. Semi (for mobile chips) as acquisitions that enhanced Apple's product ecosystem, rather than acquiring competing businesses outright.

title: Boyd Gaming capitalizing on Stardust name with new app
summary: Boyd Gaming has launched the "Stardust Social Casino" mobile app, leveraging the iconic Stardust brand to engage users with free digital games and integrate with its "B Connected" loyalty program. This move aims to capitalize on the Stardust's enduring popularity and expand Boyd Gaming's presence in the digital marketplace, especially with interactive gaming and mobile sports betting. The company views the app as a "win-win" for continuous customer engagement and hints at further plans for the brand.

title: Facebook closes on massive NYC office expansion
summary: Facebook has finalized a deal to lease 730,000 square feet at Vornado's Farley Building in New York City, marking the biggest office lease of the year. This expansion, despite earlier skepticism due to the coronavirus pandemic and Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg's work-from-home predictions, signals a strong commitment to New York City's office market. The move is seen as a testament to the city's appeal as a tech hub and a boost for efforts to revitalize central office districts.

title: Chinese artificial intelligence company files $1.4 billion lawsuit against Apple
summary: Chinese artificial intelligence company Xiao-i has filed a lawsuit against Apple Inc., seeking 10 billion yuan ($1.43 billion) in damages. Xiao-i alleges that Apple's Siri voice-recognition technology infringes on a patent it secured in 2009. This lawsuit is a continuation of a nearly decade-long dispute between the two companies over patent infringement.

title: Google buys $450M stake in ADT to give Nest a new perch
summary: Google is investing $450 million for a nearly 7% stake in ADT Inc., aiming to expand the reach of its Nest cameras and voice assistant. As part of this partnership, ADT will integrate Nest's internet-connected cameras and Nest Home Hub into its security systems. This deal allows Google to further develop its home management product line and benefit from ADT's extensive customer base.

title: Tim Cook Says These 3 Words Guide Every Decision at Apple
summary: Tim Cook stated that "privacy, security, and quality" guide every decision at Apple, especially in its app review process. The article argues that these three words differentiate Apple from its competitors, particularly concerning data privacy and product experience. It emphasizes that these principles provide clarity for Apple's decisions and are foundational to its operations, serving as a lesson for other leaders.

title: Apple Cost of Sales by Year: FY 1990 - 2020
summary: This article presents Apple's cost of sales data from fiscal year 1990 to 2020, highlighting an annual decline of 1.2% in 2019 to $161,782 million, following an all-time high of $163,756 million in FY'18. It also provides a brief overview of Apple Inc.'s history, including its founding, key products like the iPhone, and its market valuation.

title: Phil Schiller advances to Apple Fellow
summary: Apple announced that Phil Schiller will become an Apple Fellow, continuing his long career that started in 1987. In this new role, he will continue to lead the App Store and Apple Events, reporting to CEO Tim Cook. Concurrently, Greg Joswiak will join the executive team as senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing, overseeing product management, marketing, and developer relations.

title: Who Is on Apple’s Board, and Why
summary: This article details the composition of Apple's board of directors, highlighting its relatively small size and stability. It introduces each board member, including Tim Cook, Art Levinson, Al Gore, Andrea Jung, Ron Sugar, Sue Wagner, and James Bell, outlining their backgrounds, key contributions, and the rationale behind their selection. The piece also touches on their compensation and significant stock holdings.

title: Ford Motor Company gets new CEO on October 1st
summary: Jim Hackett is retiring as CEO of Ford Motor Company after three years, with current Chief Operating Officer Jim Farley taking over on October 1st, 2020. Farley aims for a 10% operating margin and acknowledges new competitors like Amazon, Baidu, Tesla, and Apple. He also faces the challenge of reviving Ford's declining car sales in China and navigating the company through the ongoing coronavirus pandemic.

title: Apple marketing chief Phil Schiller steps down from role
summary: Phil Schiller, Apple's long-serving marketing boss, is stepping down from his role but will remain with the company as an "Apple Fellow," continuing to oversee the App Store and company events. Greg Joswiak, one of Schiller's deputies, will take over as vice president of worldwide marketing. Schiller's transition marks another high-profile executive change at Apple, coming amidst increased scrutiny over the App Store's policies.

title: Oprah Winfrey names “Caste: The Origins of Our Discontents” her most important Book Club selection ever
summary: Oprah Winfrey has chosen Isabel Wilkerson's "Caste: The Origins of Our Discontents" as her most important Book Club selection to date. The book, available on Apple Books, explores America's hierarchical structure and will be accompanied by an exclusive excerpt narrated by Winfrey and a discussion with Wilkerson on Apple TV+. Winfrey will also serve as Apple News's first-ever guest editor, curating related content.

title: Apple iPhone Revenue by Year: FY 2007 – 2020
summary: This article presents Apple iPhone revenue data from fiscal year 2007 to 2020, highlighting a significant 14.6% year-over-year decline in fiscal 2019 revenue to $142,381 million due to decreased iPhone sales. It also provides background information on Apple Inc., its founding, key product launches including the first iPhone, and its valuation as one of the world's most valuable brands.

title: Disney Quarterly Earnings: Parks Lose $2 Billion, WDW Attendance Down & More
summary: The Walt Disney Company reported its Q3 2020 earnings, revealing significant losses, especially for the Parks, Resorts & Experiences division, which lost $2 billion. Despite a revenue decrease of 42% year-over-year, Disney's stock saw an after-hours bump, and Disney+ exceeded revised subscriber expectations, reaching 60.5 million. The company is weathering the financial storm with $23 billion in cash and is adapting to challenges, including lower-than-expected Walt Disney World attendance, by optimizing operations despite reduced CapEx and potential long-term recovery in destination travel.

title: Ford CEO Jim Hackett to retire; Chief Operating Officer Jim Farley will take helm
summary: Ford Motor Co. CEO Jim Hackett is retiring from his position, effective October 1, 2020, and will be succeeded by Chief Operating Officer Jim Farley. Hackett led the company since May 2017, overseeing a restructuring plan and challenges with product launches and stock value, while Farley is known as a "car guy" with a strong background in the auto industry and a focus on flawless product execution and an expanded affordable lineup. The transition comes as Ford faces intense competition and an evolving industry landscape, with many analysts and employees expressing optimism about Farley's leadership.

title: Ford's New CEO Names Amazon, Apple, Tesla, Baidu As Biggest Rivals
summary: Ford's incoming CEO, Jim Farley, has identified tech giants Amazon, Apple, Baidu, and Tesla, alongside Toyota, as the company's primary competitors, shifting focus away from traditional auto rivals like General Motors and Fiat Chrysler. Industry experts agree with Farley's assessment, noting significant investments by Silicon Valley companies in electric and self-driving vehicle technology. This new competitive landscape highlights the evolving nature of the automotive industry, demanding Ford to compete for talent and technological advancement against these innovative firms.

title: Buffett's Berkshire bought $2.07 billion BofA stock since mid-July, has 11.9% stake
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc. has acquired an additional $2.07 billion in Bank of America Corp. shares since mid-July, increasing its stake to 11.9%. The move follows regulatory approval from the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond to boost its holding up to 24.9% and helps Berkshire reduce its substantial cash reserves. This makes Bank of America Berkshire's largest common stock holding after Apple Inc.

title: Bank OZK Seeks to Foreclose on David Edelstein’s Lincoln Road Buildings
summary: Bank OZK is seeking to foreclose on two Lincoln Road properties owned by developer David Edelstein, looking to collect on the remaining $12.8 million of a loan plus fees and interest. The suit alleges that loan guarantors, including Edelstein's TriStar Capital, have not made a payment since April. The bank's action highlights early commercial foreclosures in South Florida amidst a challenging period for Lincoln Road businesses.

title: Get Long Alibaba Stock Into Earnings With Confidence
summary: This article suggests investors consider going long on Alibaba (BABA) stock, despite market volatility and potential risks like U.S.-China rhetoric. It highlights BABA's strong recovery post-quarantine and its status as a superstar stock, comparable to other tech giants. The author recommends using options strategies, specifically selling puts, to enter positions with managed risk ahead of earnings.

title: Buffett buys back record $5.1 billion in Berkshire stock as coronavirus hits operating earnings
summary: Berkshire Hathaway repurchased a record $5.1 billion of its own stock in May and June, the largest single buyback period for Warren Buffett's conglomerate. This occurred as operating profits fell 10% in the second quarter due to the coronavirus pandemic impacting businesses like Geico and Precision Castparts, though net earnings surged to $26.3 billion primarily from unrealized gains in public market investments. Buffett warned against focusing solely on these volatile net earnings due to the pandemic's ongoing uncertainties.

title: Chicago looting update: Lincoln Park Apple store, Best Buy destroyed in North Clybourn business district shopping center
summary: A Lincoln Park shopping center in Chicago was heavily targeted by looters overnight, leading to significant destruction at stores like Apple and Best Buy. Residents and volunteers actively participated in cleanup efforts, expressing dismay over the repeated incidents of looting and the negative impact on the city's image, following similar unrest in June. The destruction left many feeling horrified and questioning their safety in the city, with cleanup acting as a coping mechanism.

title: |【2020最新】知的好奇心を刺激するアート(芸術)系アプリのおすすめ5選
summary: This article introduces five recommended art-related apps from 2020 that stimulate intellectual curiosity. It highlights apps like "DailyArt" for daily art discovery, "Ukiyo-e Wallpaper" for Japanese art backgrounds, "Magic Poser" for 3D model drawing references, "Chirashi Museum" for event leaflets, and "Happy Color" for number-based coloring puzzles. The article details features and benefits of each app, catering to both art education and entertainment.

title: Apple’s Employee Uniforms Tied to Forced Labor in Xinjiang
summary: A Tech Transparency Project (TTP) investigation reveals that Apple's employee uniforms are sourced from Esquel Group, a company sanctioned by the U.S. government in July 2020 for its involvement in forced labor and human rights abuses in China’s Xinjiang region. This finding undermines Apple's claims of having "zero tolerance" for forced labor in its supply chain. Despite Apple's denial of direct sourcing from Esquel, shipping records and industry reports suggest a long-standing relationship and reliance on Xinjiang cotton, highlighting Apple's entanglement with problematic labor practices in China.

title: Apple Countersues Stereo Headphone Inventor Koss Over Patent Lawsuit
summary: Apple has countersued stereo headphone inventor and manufacturer Koss over a patent lawsuit accusing Apple and other companies of violating patents related to wireless headphone technology. Apple claims Koss's allegations are baseless and that the lawsuit breaks a confidentiality agreement from 2017. Apple also submitted evidence to refute Koss's claims of patent infringement.

title: FuboTV begins streaming some content in 4K with HDR10
summary: FuboTV has started streaming select content, specifically main broadcasts of the 2018 FIFA World Cup, in 4K resolution with HDR10 support. This feature is initially available on Chromecast and Amazon Fire TV 4K devices, with support for Apple TV and Roku devices coming soon. FuboTV is the first virtual MVPD to launch 4K HDR in beta, requiring users to have compatible 4K HDR TVs, HDMI 2.0/2.2 ports, and sufficient bandwidth.

title: Mudra Band: Gesture control wristband for the Apple Watch raises over US$170,000 in crowdfunding
summary: The Mudra Band, a gesture control wristband for the Apple Watch developed by Wearable Devices Ltd, has successfully raised over US$170,000 in crowdfunding. This innovative accessory interprets nerve signals to enable gesture controls for the Apple Watch Series 3 and newer, connecting via Bluetooth. It promises over two days of battery life and is currently available for pre-order at US$159, with an expected retail price of US$249.

title: [Interview] Manga platform Piccoma ready to take over Japan's comics market
summary: Piccoma, a manga platform by Kakao Japan, is rapidly expanding in Japan's digital comics market, becoming the top-grossing non-gaming app in July. Despite a late start, Piccoma's focus on Korean webtoons has driven significant revenue growth, making it a frontrunner in the world's largest comics market. The company plans to enhance content quality, user experience through big data and AI, and is preparing for an IPO to fund its continued growth and market dominance.
